findings.title: Money requested before any viewing
findings.detail: The agent asks for money before you have seen the property in person. Paying before a viewing is the most common way students lose a deposit.

findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The arithmetic is not disputed: GBP 1300 x 12 = GBP 15,600 a year, which gives a five-week cap of GBP 1,500.00. The stated deposit of GBP 1500 equals the cap and does not exceed it. This is a correctly limited amount-cap pass, not a breach. The cap only applies to covered tenancies. The supplied context leaves jurisdiction, tenancy type and rent basis as "unknown". The property address is in London, but that does not settle whether this is an ordinary private tenancy rather than an excluded arrangement. Nothing in the contract contradicts the rent or deposit figures. No supplied quote defeats this reading, so dismissal is not available. The result says nothing about deposit protection or the authenticity of the contract or parties. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

findings.title: What the messages actually state
findings.detail: • The student asks to view Flat 2, 20 Example Mews on 15 November 2026 at 16:00 before paying. • The owner, Mira Vale, is abroad. • Viewing is not possible until payment is made. • Payment is requested as GBP 1500 in prepaid gift cards, with redemption codes sent. • The deadline for sending the codes is 16 November 2026 at 18:00. • The contract names Mira Vale and lists Rowan Pike as the managing agent. • The agent says the gift card codes are their reservation system. • The agent says there is no bank transfer alternative. • The agent says no viewing is possible before the codes arrive.
